- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce peak value by 2–5% to account for mean reversion or volatility decay.
- In periods with strong upward sentiment (avg > 0.15), model often overestimates future price; apply downward bias of 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after a dip, model frequently lags; add 1–2 days of gradual upward slope to forecast to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (avg ±0.1), model tends to overfit recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values to reduce false peaks.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often underestimates late-period spikes; increase final 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–3% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum or policy surprises.
